vyrn library reference 0.1.0

Everything your scripts can use. Start a script with import vyrn, then call these in inputs.py, responses.py, points.py and world.py. In the editor, press F1 on a vyrn. name to jump here.

vyrn.screen(x=None, y=None, width=None, height=None)Picture of an area of the screen; with no numbers, the whole screen.
vyrn.pixel(x, y)Color of one screen pixel as (red, green, blue), each 0-255.
vyrn.on_screen(name, x=None, y=None, match=0.9)True if the Snapshot picture called name is showing at x, y on the screen right now.
vyrn.press(key)Tap a key (or a combo like "ctrl+c") right now, e.g. in restart(): vyrn.press("space").
vyrn.wait(seconds)Pause for this many seconds, e.g. vyrn.wait(0.5) to give a game time to restart.
vyrn.canvas(width, height, color="black")A blank picture to draw on: picture.dot(x, y, color) and picture.box(x, y, width, height, color).
vyrn.show(name, value)Show a number, text or picture on the dashboard under this name, e.g. vyrn.show("speed", 3.5).
vyrn.send(type, **fields)Send a message to the game now, like vyrn.send("restart") or vyrn.send("speed", value=2.0).
vyrn.choiceThe choice the AI made last in this round, like "left" (None at the start of a round).
vyrn.tickTicks since this round started (0 on the round's first see()).
vyrn.roundThe round number, starting at 1 (0 while your scripts load).
vyrn.gameThe newest state from a game connected with Vyrn Link: a dict like {"y": 105.0, "dead": False}.
vyrn.eventsThe game's events since the last tick, oldest first, like [{"type": "event", "name": "death"}].
vyrn.connectedTrue while a game is connected with Vyrn Link.
picture.dot(x, y, color="white")Color one pixel: x counts columns from the left, y counts rows from the top.
picture.box(x, y, width, height, color="white")Fill a rectangle whose top-left corner is (x, y).

Functions

Call these from your scripts.

vyrn.screen(x=None, y=None, width=None, height=None)

Picture of an area of the screen; with no numbers, the whole screen.

x, y is the area's top-left corner and width, height its size, in screen pixels. Toolbar → Pick area fills these in for you. The result is a picture: a numpy array of shape [height, width, 3] (red, green, blue).

Example

def see():
    return vyrn.screen(x=0, y=0, width=640, height=480)

vyrn.pixel(x, y)

Color of one screen pixel as (red, green, blue), each 0-255.

Example

r, g, b = vyrn.pixel(20, 20)
return r > 200 and g < 80      # is it red?

vyrn.on_screen(name, x=None, y=None, match=0.9)

True if the Snapshot picture called name is showing at x, y on the screen right now.

Take Snapshots with toolbar → Snapshot; they are saved in your project's pictures folder. Leave out x and y to look where the Snapshot was taken. match is how alike they must be: 1.0 means exactly, 0.9 (the default) allows small changes.

Example

def game_over():
    return vyrn.on_screen("game_over.png")

vyrn.press(key)

Tap a key (or a combo like "ctrl+c") right now, e.g. in restart(): vyrn.press("space").

Keys can only be pressed while the AI plays (Train or Watch) and your game window is active.

vyrn.wait(seconds)

Pause for this many seconds, e.g. vyrn.wait(0.5) to give a game time to restart.

vyrn.canvas(width, height, color="black")

A blank picture to draw on: picture.dot(x, y, color) and picture.box(x, y, width, height, color).

Example

picture = vyrn.canvas(10, 10)
picture.dot(3, 4, "white")
return picture

vyrn.show(name, value)

Show a number, text or picture on the dashboard under this name, e.g. vyrn.show("speed", 3.5).

vyrn.send(type, **fields)

Send a message to the game now, like vyrn.send("restart") or vyrn.send("speed", value=2.0).

The game gets {"type": "restart"} or {"type": "speed", "value": 2.0}, and its mod decides what to do with them (the Geometry Dash mod restarts the level on "restart"). Values can be numbers, text, True/False, None, and lists or dicts of those. It works with a game connected with Vyrn Link, for example in restart():

Example

def restart():
    vyrn.send("restart")

What is happening now

Vyrn keeps these up to date while the AI plays; just read them.

vyrn.choice

The choice the AI made last in this round, like "left" (None at the start of a round).

Write vyrn.choice: "from vyrn import choice" copies it once, so it never changes.

vyrn.tick

Ticks since this round started (0 on the round's first see()).

Write vyrn.tick: "from vyrn import tick" copies it once, so it never changes.

vyrn.round

The round number, starting at 1 (0 while your scripts load).

Write vyrn.round: "from vyrn import round" copies it once, and hides Python's own round().

vyrn.game

The newest state from a game connected with Vyrn Link: a dict like {"y": 105.0, "dead": False}.

It is {} until the game sends a state, so read it with .get(): vyrn.game.get("y", 0). Write vyrn.game: "from vyrn import game" copies it once, so it never changes.

vyrn.events

The game's events since the last tick, oldest first, like [{"type": "event", "name": "death"}].

Write vyrn.events: "from vyrn import events" copies it once, so it never changes.

vyrn.connected

True while a game is connected with Vyrn Link.

Write vyrn.connected: "from vyrn import connected" copies it once, so it never changes.

Drawing on a canvas

A picture from vyrn.canvas() has these methods, for example picture = vyrn.canvas(10, 10) then picture.dot(3, 4, "white"). x counts columns from the left and y rows from the top; drawing off the edge is simply left out.

picture.dot(x, y, color="white")

Color one pixel: x counts columns from the left, y counts rows from the top.

picture.box(x, y, width, height, color="white")

Fill a rectangle whose top-left corner is (x, y).

Made from the vyrn library's own docstrings (python/vyrn/__init__.py).
